2.note: FIRST DIVERGENCE: the third solution (the O(log^2 n) one, the only full-credit tier) is wrong as printed. Own sim on near-complete trees n<400: (i) the step 3 test 'left-mid length = right-mid length = h returns 0' fires for incomplete trees (n=6, 12, 13, 14, 24, ...); (ii) step 10 compares h1 with h0 AFTER step 9 decrements h0, off by one: it needs the compare before the decrement. With the completeness test replaced by 'rightmost path length = h' AND the compare before the decrement, 0 mismatches for n<400; with either printed error 136 to 383 mismatches. The linear solution (h from left path, n by inorder, 2^(h+1)-1-n) is correct; the O(min(n,d log n)) solution is correct if the path encoding is read as (h-1)-bit padded, bit 0 = right, bit 1 = left, i from 0 (stated: 'depth = length-1' is not literally consistent). Rubric 5+5+8+7=25 awards the full 25 to the O(n) solution, but the question gives full marks only to O(log^2 n) and reduced marks to O(n). Steps agree (left path, 2^4-1-10=5, 2^4-1-8=7, Theta(n)).

3a.note: Own AVL sim: no rotation for 3,1,7,0,6,9,5,8,10 (height 3); inserting 11 gives balance -2 at the root, right child 7 has -1 -> single left rotation, new root 7: 7(3(1(0),6(5)),9(8,10(.,11))). Matches pages 7-8 of the official solution. Steps agree (0 rotations, -2, option a, root 7). Rubric 4+3+3=10.

3b.note: FIRST DIVERGENCE (statement level): the printed 'levels 0..ceil(h/2) are full' is FALSE for every odd h (h=1: root plus one child, level 1 has 1 node, not 2; h=3, 5, 7, 9 likewise). Own exhaustive level-count DP over all AVL trees, heights 0..9: the guaranteed full prefix is exactly levels 0..floor(h/2), which is the exam's own formal clause 'for all 0<=i<=h/2'. So the exam question is internally inconsistent (prose ceil vs formal i<=h/2), and the official proof, which carries ceil all the way (1+ceil((h-1)/2)=ceil((h+1)/2), arithmetic correct) proves a false statement: base case h=0 only, and the step breaks at h+1=1 (lighter subtree can be empty) and so every odd height inherits the false bound. This is a final-answer error in the official solution, not an intermediate slip; the true theorem needs floor(h/2) (step: 1+floor((h-1)/2)=floor((h+1)/2) for h>=1, handle h+1=1 separately). Needs a הערה explaining that the formal clause i<=h/2 (floor) is what is proven; the stored solution/steps (order, findbug, numeric) teach the false ceil version. Arithmetic in each step is itself correct. Rubric 2+2+4+3+4=15.
